newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends strong, Sept near one-year highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends strong, Sept near one-year highs.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed strongly on Friday, with September climbing to a near one-year high amid heavy trade and fund buying.

Septmber peaked at 1,134 stg per tonne, the highest since June 19, 1996 and a fresh contract high, before slipping back on profit-taking and light origin sales in forward months. September closed up 31 at 1,127.
Front-month July also scored a new contract high of 1,122 before a late wave of profit-taking cut gains. July ended up 40 at 1,116.

London cocoa was already firm at midday as funds and trade bought on every profit-taking dip. But it got an added boost when New York opened sharply higher and CSCE September raced to a lifetime high on fund buying.

The rally extended Thursday's surge on concerns the developing El Nino weather pattern would spark droughts in major cocoa-producing countries and disrupt next year's cocoa crop. There was also talk that early Ivory Coast settings for the new crop remained low.

Though some traders were sceptical of the fundamental change said to be pushing cocoa prices higher, they said they could not ignore the strong uptrend developing on near- and intermediate-term technical charts.

Bullish technical signs were seen luring funds and speculators looking for an eventual move to September's initial resistances at 1,142 and 1,165. If September clears those levels, some technical analysts said they could see the start of a longer-term bull trend sending September as high as 1,300.
Technical analysts were also encouraged by the hefty volume in the recent upswing. Thursday's turnover was the highest since March 31, 1995, and Friday traded a bulky 23,714 contracts.
The heavy volume was seen underlining the strength of the up move, analysts said.
If prices turnaround, analysts said September support rested much below the market at 1,046, the June 11 high and the bottom of a chart gap left from the following day's low of 1,059.
Despite the active futures market, options remained lackluster. Ten September 1,100 calls and 25 September 1,200 calls changed hands in the afternoon.
